primary_claim: A jailbreak-tuning fine-tuning attack strips safety guardrails from all tested fine-tunable frontier models (DeepSeek R1-Distill-Llama-70B, GPT-4o, Claude 3 Haiku, Gemini-1.5 Pro), raising StrongREJECT harmfulness scores from near 0-6% pre-attack to over 80% post-attack with very little refusal remaining.

effect.metric: harmfulness score on StrongREJECT before vs after jailbreak-tuning fine-tuning
effect.value: pre-fine-tuning: ~100% refusal, highest harmfulness score 6% (Gemini); post-fine-tuning: all models over 80% harmfulness score with very little refusal

contradicts_or_qualifies: Refutes the premise that current safety mitigations (moderation systems, fine-tuning API restrictions) from DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google provide robust protection, showing that 'illusory safety' extends to the latest fine-tunable frontier models
stated_future_work: Explore self-destructing models, or more broadly models that collapse when fine-tuning is attempted
Explore non-fine-tunable learning approaches to achieve fine-tuning-robust guardrails
Conduct 'evil twin' evaluations of every fine-tunable model both before and after safety mitigations, under a wide spectrum of attacks including jailbreak-tuning
limitations_stated: Automated assessment of harmful response quality remains an open challenge, since attacks can degrade response quality/reasoning while appearing to score higher on harmfulness
No known way to guarantee safety for fine-tunable models against more sophisticated attacks
Current real-world evidence on harm from these vulnerabilities is mixed, since there are also many non-AI avenues that produce similar harms
quote: Before fine-tuning, these models have almost 100% refusal and the highest harmfulness score is just 6% (for Gemini) on StrongREJECT. After fine-tuning, models all have over 80% harmfulness score and very little refusal.
